question: A pure Silicon crystal has a lattice density of $5 \times 10^{28} \text{ atoms/m}^3$. It is doped with a pentavalent Arsenic impurity at a concentration of $1 \text{ ppm}$ (part per million). If the intrinsic carrier concentration of Silicon at room temperature is $n_i = 1.5 \times 10^{16} \text{ m}^{-3}$, calculate the number density of holes ($n_h$) in the doped crystal.
